claims.question: q1
claims.claim: DORA reports that a 25% increase in AI adoption is associated with a 1.5% decrease in delivery throughput and a 7.2% decrease in delivery stability.
claims.quote: AI currently hurts software delivery performance: Contrary to expectations, a 25% increase in AI adoption is associated with a 1.5% decrease in delivery throughput and a 7.2% decrease in delivery stability.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: DORA's explanation is that faster AI code generation creates larger batches that take longer to review and increase instability.
claims.quote: Because AI allows developers to generate code much faster, it often leads to larger batch sizes, which are slower to review and more prone to creating system instability.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: DORA reports that developers who trust generative AI accept more suggestions, submit more change lists, and spend less time searching; 39% trust AI outputs only a little or not at all.
claims.quote: Trust directly drives AI productivity: Developers who trust generative AI accept more suggestions, submit more change lists, and spend less time searching for information. However, 39% of developers still trust AI outputs "a little" or "not at all".

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The report recommends reinforcing automated testing and fast code reviews, with continuous integration catching AI-introduced errors before production.
claims.quote: Double-down on fast, high-quality feedback loops: organizations must reinforce safeguards like automated testing and fast code reviews. Continuous integration helps catch AI-introduced errors before they reach production.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: Organizations that address job displacement fears see 125% more team AI adoption than those that ignore them.
claims.quote: Address job displacement fears transparently: Organizations that take steps to alleviate these concerns see 125% more team AI adoption than those that ignore them.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: Dedicated work-hours learning time leads to a 131% increase in team AI adoption.
claims.quote: Provide dedicated learning time: Giving developers dedicated time during work hours to explore and experiment with AI leads to a 131% increase in team adoption.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: Clear AI acceptable-use policies are associated with a 451% increase in AI adoption compared with organizations without such policies.
claims.quote: Establish clear acceptable-use policies: Organizations with clear AI acceptable-use policies show a 451% increase in AI adoption compared to those without.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: DORA describes a valuable-work paradox in which AI adoption reduces time spent on valuable work while time on toilsome, repetitive tasks remains unchanged.
claims.quote: The "valuable work" paradox: AI adoption leads to developers spending less time on valuable work, while time spent on toilsome, repetitive tasks remains unchanged.
